title: Revenue shock: hiring latency & pricing protocol
content:
Purpose:
This is a rapid-response protocol for scenarios where net revenue (or token consumption) drops sharply over 2+ consecutive weeks (we use a 15%+ week-over-week decline threshold). The doc ties together: hiring/stop-start latency, near-term price moves, and headcount redistribution to preserve runway while protecting SLA-critical paths.

Scope:
- Finance + People Ops + Product + Sales (pricing ops) coordination for 0–12 weeks after shock onset.
- Focused on hosted API and Dedicated routes where usage is visible and price elasticity can be adjusted quickly.
- Does NOT attempt model-architecture changes or large quantization programs (those are separate tracks).

Key assumptions (defaults unless overridden):
- Average token price sensitivity: small/medium customers 1.8 elasticity, enterprise 0.8–1.1.
- Hiring latency: 6–8 weeks to hire for senior infra/serving roles; 2–4 weeks to pause/contract onboarding for junior roles.
- Fixed monthly cost per FTE (all-in loaded): engineers $18k, infra engineers $20k, support $12k, solutions eng $16k, sales $14k.
- Burst capacity (GPU) cost managed via reserved vs spot. Bursting can be throttled to save ~35% of immediate GPU marginal spend but increases latency risk.

Scenario matrix (simplified):
- Shallow dip: -15% vol, lasts 4–8 weeks.
  - Goal: temporary pricing nudges + hiring freeze for non-critical reqs.
- Mid dip: -30% vol, 6–12 weeks.
  - Goal: targeted price increases per-cohort + reassign contractors, pause certain opens.
- Deep dip: -50% vol or prolonged >12 weeks.
  - Goal: combination of tiered price increases, conservative HC reductions, and renegotiation of committed capacity with vendors.

Headcount sensitivity table (quick view):
Role | Current FTE | Criticality | Stop-start latency (weeks) | Monthly loaded cost
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
Serving runtime eng | 22 | Very High | 6–8 | $20,000
Platform infra | 14 | High | 6–8 | $20,000
Product (hosted API) | 10 | High | 4–6 | $18,000
Solutions & SE | 8 | Medium | 3–4 | $16,000
Support (L1/L2) | 12 | Medium | 2–3 | $12,000
Sales (field) | 18 | Medium | 4–6 | $14,000
Recruiting/TA | 3 | Low | 1–2 | $10,000
Contractors & Temp | ~20 (var) | Low-Med | 0–2 | $8,000 avg

Example headcount levers and near-term impact (numbers illustrative):
- Pause new external hiring (all non-critical reqs): immediate hiring cost saving = open req OTE runway * pro-rated months. Rough rule: pausing 10 reqs = ~$160k/mo saved (assuming $16k/mo loaded).
- Convert open reqs to contractors (where latency allows): reduces ramp time but increases per-hour cost; net short-term savings vary.
- Pause contractor renewals: immediate monthly savings (e.g., drop 8 contractors = $64k/mo).

Pricing sensitivity quick-calcs (back-of-envelope):
Inputs: baseline revenue R0, elasticities per cohort E_c, mix m_c (fraction of revenue).
Delta revenue if price change p%: 
  Revenue_new = sum_c (R0*m_c*(1 + p) * (1 + p)^{E_c})  // crude multiplicative approximation
Practical guidance: small price steps (3–7%) targeted to low-risk cohorts (enterprise feature tiers, per-seat contracts) before broad API-per-token increases.

Simple worked example (mid-dip):
- Baseline monthly hosted revenue: $4,000,000. Mix: enterprise 40% (E=0.9), startups 45% (E=1.9), partners 15% (E=1.3).
- Option: +5% price only to startups cohort.
  Startups revenue contribution = 0.45 * 4M = 1.8M. With E=1.9, demand drop ~9% => new startups revenue ~1.8M * 1.05 * 0.91 = ~1.72M (net +20k).
  Net platform effect small; combine with contract-level discounts removal and enrollment caps for better impact.

Decision triggers (quantitative):
1) If weekly token volume decreases >=15% for 2 consecutive weeks -> convene Finance Ops standup (24h).
2) If burn delta >$500k/mo vs plan -> pull pricing lever A (targeted cohort adjustments) + hiring freeze except critical roles.
3) If booking velocity declines >30% and pipeline conversion <50% of baseline -> escalate to GTM for targeted retention credits + HC redeployment.

Operational playbook (first 0–2 weeks):
- Day 0–2: Finance Ops call, snapshot metrics, assign owners. (Owner: Maya P., Ops lead: Ethan M.)
- Day 2–7: Implement hiring freeze for all non-critical reqs; pause contractor renewals >30 days out. (People Ops).
- Day 3–10: Price experiment: +3–5% targeted to 2 low-risk cohorts; monitor elasticity hourly/daily. (GTM + Pricing Ops).
- Day 7–14: If revenue still below threshold, start vendor capacity renegotiation (Reserved vs Spot swap) and prioritize latency-SLO routes for retention. (Infra + Legal).

Action tiles (owner / ETA / acceptance criteria):
- People Ops: produce list of open reqs ranked by stop-start latency and criticality (ETA 48h). Accepted = list with suggested pause/pursue flag.
- Finance: produce 6-week cash runway delta given proposed HC moves and price steps (ETA 72h). Accepted = model with sensitivities.
- GTM: roll targeted price step to startups cohort on staging and measure 7-day elasticity (ETA 5 days). Accepted = cohort metrics (churn delta, MRR delta).
- Infra: snapshot burst GPU spend and estimate savings if burst throttled 25/50% (ETA 5 days). Accepted = clear estimate and risk notes.

Risk notes and guardrails:
- Avoid sweeping per-token hikes on all hosted routes in first 2 weeks — high churn risk and poor PR optics.
- Protect serving-runtime headcount to avoid SLA breaches: moving from 22 -> 18 has outsized latency risk.
- When pausing hires, include explicit re-opportunity windows (e.g., review at 4-week intervals).

Open questions (for execs / People Ops / Legal):
- What is the desired public comms posture if we implement broad pricing changes mid-quarter? (Legal/Comms)
- Which contract clauses allow temporary increases for marketplace partners? (Legal/GTM)
- Can we accelerate internal transfers (SE -> Support) without severance impacts? (People Ops)

Next steps:
1) Confirm owners and meeting cadence for immediate Finance Ops standup.
2) People Ops to produce pauseable-reqs list (48h).
3) Finance to run quick sensitivity model for 0/3/6/12 week horizons (+/- price steps of 3/5/10%).
4) GTM to prepare cohort-targeted pricing experiment and retention credit options.

Notes-to-self (scratch):
- Track token mix changes daily; if startups share falls <30% of baseline mix, consider broader discount removal.
- Keep a simple public-facing FAQ ready if customers ask about price changes (avoid surprise).

References / bookmarks:
- CONFLUENCE-OPS-1442 (capacity & burst playbook)
- JIRA-FIN-1721 (sensitivity model spreadsheet)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/898 (metric pipeline change)

Status: draft — intended as an operational checklist and sensitivity primer for the immediate 0–12 week window after a revenue shock.

Unresolved: will iterate after the first live experiment and the People Ops pause list arrives.
